channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Experts React to Cochrane Findings
item.description: Expert reaction to the latest Cochrane findings should move the vaping debate closer to clinical reality. Nicotine vapes have stronger evidence for helping people quit smoking than many critics are willing to acknowledge, especially for adults who have struggled with other methods. That does not make vaping risk-free or suitable for non-smokers. It means cessation advice should reflect the evidence clearly enough to help smokers leave combustion behind. (Published on September 02, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: The US is moving fast on pouches, the EU should follow its lead
item.description: The US approach to nicotine pouches shows a more practical way to handle smoke-free innovation. Rather than treating the category as a threat by default, regulators can assess products through evidence, standards and their potential role in moving adults away from cigarettes. Europe should not fall behind by regulating pouches as though all nicotine use carries the same public health meaning. A risk-proportionate framework would protect young people while allowing lower-risk alternatives to compete with combustible tobacco. (Published on September 02, 2026byworldvapersalliance.com)

item.title: Bans Don’t Eliminate Demand! | GFN Voices 2026 #6
item.description: Bans can remove legal access, but they do not remove demand. Nicotine markets continue through informal supply, cross-border purchasing and illicit sellers once regulated options are pushed out of reach. That leaves consumers with fewer safeguards and authorities with less control. Harm reduction works better by shaping demand through legal, accountable routes than by pretending demand can be legislated away. (Published on September 03, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Tobacco Control Advocates: Big Tobacco’s Useful Idiots
item.description: Tobacco control loses credibility when opposition to industry turns into opposition to harm reduction itself. Cigarette companies deserve scrutiny, but that does not make every argument for safer nicotine products a tobacco industry tactic. Adult smokers are poorly served by a debate that treats reduced-risk options as contamination rather than opportunity. Public health should be able to reject industry misconduct while still recognising evidence that helps people move away from combustion. (Published on September 03, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)
